detail.body:
## Overview

  Makes DeepSeek-V4.1's per-layer decode attention step **1.4-2.15x faster** for decode steps of up to 16 tokens at TP2 / TP4, by adding a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention kernel to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer (#56935) on SM10x. Steps of up to 16
  tokens with 16 or 32 live heads per rank (TP4 / TP2 of the 64-head model) now take it instead of the mega kernel, which pads the heads to 64.
  Part of #57448; it reads the interleaved V4.1 KV records from #61371. Related work that this PR does not duplicate (see Details): #59418, #61615, #57711, #61868.

  ## Claims

  - **1.4-2.15x faster decode attention for 1-16 tokens:** 1.8-2.15x with 16 live heads (TP4) and 1.4-1.8x with 32 (TP2), for both NVFP4 and fp8 compressed records (per-layer Q pad + KV insert + attention, table below; the lower ends are B300). End to end at TP2 this is 4.5-7.6% lower median TPOT at concurrency 1-16 (see the A/B comment). The mega kernel's FP8 decode maps
  query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads; swap-AB puts the KV slots on M and only the live heads on N.
  - **Accuracy:** the output's error against an fp64 reference is at most 1.1x the mega kernel's, and the output is within 2% of the mega kernel's, over 64 test cases.
  - **Automatic and contained.** There is no new flag, environment variable or config option. Every other decode step, layer and TP size keeps the mega kernel; prefill and other platforms are unchanged. The new kernel is CUDA-graph safe and deterministic,
  and adds no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Performance.** This PR adds a swap-AB arm to the existing `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`. Each arm's per-step ops (Q pad + KV insert + attention) are timed as a CUDA graph replay, the same harness that produced the mega vs split-KV
  table in `flash_mla_mega_attn.py`.

  ```bash
  for heads in 16 32; do
    for rec in 288 528; do
      .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py \
          --local-heads $heads --extra-bytes $rec --decode-s-q 1 2 4 8 16 32 64
    done
  done
  ```

  Speedup = mega step time / swap-AB step time (median of two runs, which differ by at most 9% per cell):

  | Live heads | Compressed record | 1 token | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 16 (TP4) | NVFP4 (288 B) | **2.15x** | **2.00x** | **2.06x** | **1.94x** | **2.04x** | 1.25x | 0.94x |
  | 16 (TP4) | fp8 (528 B) | **2.13x** | **1.96x** | **2.02x** | **1.90x** | **1.99x** | 1.22x | 0.91x |
  | 32 (TP2) | fp8 (528 B) | **1.76x** | **1.66x** | **1.71x** | **1.62x** | **1.71x** | 0.98x | 0.73x |

  At 32 tokens swap-AB still wins with 16 heads (1.22-1.25x) but only breaks even with 32 (0.98-1.02x), and at 64 it loses with both, so `_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS = 16` is the largest step size where it wins for both head counts. On B300 (nightly 76c6f3f2) the same harness gives 1.83-2.0x with 16 heads and 1.41-1.64x with 32 heads at 1-16 tokens, for both record formats. As in the existing harness,
  every replay reuses the same buffers, so the KV reads hit a warm L2 for both kernels; timed alone with the L2 flushed before every call, the attention kernel is 1.6-2.3x faster than the mega kernel over 48 shapes with 1-16 tokens (geomean 1.94x).

  **Correctness: unit tests.** The kernel tests skip unless the GPU is SM10x and the CuTe DSL is built with CUDA 13.2+.

  ```bash
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_swapab_decode.py
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode"
  ```

  | Test (cases) | Checks | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `test_matches_reference` (64) | 16/32 heads x 1/2/5/16 tokens x NVFP4/fp8 compressed records x 64/128-slot pages x partial/full lengths. Output is finite; Frobenius and max-abs error vs an fp64 reference are <= 1.1x the mega kernel's; within 2% of the
  mega output | 64 passed |
  | `test_untouched_padding` (2) | Padding heads' output groups keep their bytes | 2 passed |
  | `test_cuda_graph_and_determinism` (12) | Repeated eager calls and a CUDA graph replay agree bit for bit, also after the inputs change in place | 12 passed |
  | `test_dispatch_rule` (9, CPU) | Which kernel each dispatch condition selects | 9 passed |
  | `test_warmup_key_matches_launch` (4, CPU) | The key the layer registers at construction is the key a decode step launches, on a compressed cache shaped as the model runner binds it | 4 passed |
  | `test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode` (3, existing) | The V4.1 cache writers and FlashMLA agree on the interleaved records the kernel reads | 3 passed |

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention is the default DeepSeek V4.1 decode path on SM10x. Its FP8 decode kernel takes 64 or 128 query heads, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads. The mega vs split-KV note in
  `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` already records that this padded-head cost dominates small decode steps. Small steps are what low-concurrency decode and spec-decode verify and draft steps run.

  **Why a separate kernel, not a FlashMLA change.** FlashMLA's decode maps query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64. Serving 16 or 32 heads without padding needs the opposite mapping, with KV slots on M and heads on N. That is a
  different kernel, not a smaller tile. In FlashMLA it would be CUDA C++ shipped through a vllm-project/FlashMLA release and a vLLM bump, as #61371 was. The CuTe DSL kernel instead compiles from Python at JIT warmup, needs no build change, and lives next
  to its only caller in the DSv4.1 model package. It is adapted from SGLang's swap-AB DSv4 decode attention (Apache-2.0, attribution in the file header).

  <details>
  <summary>Kernel design</summary>

  - **MMA shape.** `SwapABDecodeKernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/swapab_decode_attn.py`) puts the KV slots on the tcgen05 MMA's M side (128 rows) and the live heads on N (16 or 32).
  - **One CTA per (token, KV tile).** Tiles are 64 slots of the SWA list or 128 slots of the compressed list. Each CTA:
    - gathers its slots' V4.1 records in place (fp8 528 B, NVFP4 288 B, each token's scales after its data);
    - dequantizes them exactly to bf16 in SMEM;
    - RoPEs Q in fp32 from the mega kernel's chunk-interleaved, head-padded layout;
    - computes S = KV Q^T and O = KV^T P, with P split into bf16 hi and lo parts.
  - **One cluster per token.** A token's tiles form one thread-block cluster: 6 CTAs for V4.1-Flash's 128-slot window plus 512 compressed slots. The cluster merges the partials and the attention sink over DSMEM in a fixed peer order. It then applies the
  inverse RoPE and writes MXFP8 with the mega kernel's rounding rule into the o-fused buffers `wo_a` reads, for the live heads' groups only.
  - **One launch.** The kernel uses PDL and has no workspace, second kernel, allocation or host sync.
  - **JIT warmup.** The compile key is (live heads, slot-list widths, compressed record size, SWA and compressed page sizes); the token count is the grid's y dimension. Every field is fixed when the layer is built: the backend has one kernel block size (128), so a compressed page always holds
  `128 // compress_ratio` slots, whatever the KV cache manager's block size. The layer registers the key in `__init__`, next to its other JIT warmups, and `kernel_warmup` compiles it before CUDA graph capture. V4.1-Flash needs two keys, one per compressed page size.

  </details>

  **Dispatch.** `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention._forward_decode_mega` takes the swap-AB kernel only when all of these hold:
  - the GPU is SM10x;
  - the layer has a compressed cache;
  - the layer has 16 or 32 live heads;
  - a token's tiles fit one portable cluster: `ceil(window / 64) + ceil(index_topk / 128) <= 8`;
  - the CuTe DSL imports and was built with CUDA 13.2+, which the direct fp8 / fp4 to bf16x2 conversions need (PTX ISA 9.2);
  - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off;
  - the step has at most 16 decode tokens (`_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS`). Under CUDA graphs this is the padded count, so each captured graph holds exactly one of the two kernels;
  - the step's SWA list is exactly the window. DSpark's non-causal draft steps widen it, so they keep the mega kernel.

  The first six conditions are fixed when the layer is built. The last two are host-side shape checks on each step. If any condition fails, the step runs the mega kernel exactly as before.
  **Complexity.** The change adds about 1,260 lines of kernel code (about 400 of them are 23 small inline-PTX wrappers) and about 100 lines in the layer. Nothing changes in the model runner, the scheduler, FlashMLA or shared attention code. At runtime the
  kernel module is imported only by SM10x layers with a compressed cache, 16 or 32 heads and an importable CuTe DSL. Most of the maintenance cost is the inline PTX and the SMEM / TMEM layout math. Both are documented next to the code, and the tests pin
  them to an fp64 reference and to the mega kernel.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - **Cost grows with tokens.** The kernel runs one cluster of up to 8 CTAs per token, and its 150+ KiB of SMEM means one CTA per SM. Hence the 16-token cutoff, which is the same for TP2 / TP4 and both record formats: in the table above swap-AB is at
  least 1.6x faster at every step size up to 16 tokens (at least 1.4x on B300).
  - **Not bit-identical.** The fp32 sums are ordered differently from the mega kernel's, so the output depends on which kernel the step size selects. Batch-invariant runs therefore keep the mega kernel at every size.
  - **Unused Q padding.** The fused KV insert still zero-pads Q to 64 heads, which swap-AB does not read. This keeps one Q contract for both kernels.
  - **Toolchain.** The kernel needs a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+. With an older build the layer keeps the mega kernel and the kernel tests skip.
  - **Startup.** V4.1-Flash adds two JIT compiles per worker, at warmup.

  **Compatibility.**
  - **Scope.** Only `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention` changes. The FlashMLA sparse layer, FlashInfer sparse MLA, and the SM90, SM120 and ROCm paths are untouched. TP1 (64 heads) and TP8 (8 heads) keep the mega kernel.
  - **Model runners.** Both V1 and V2 build the model under the JIT warmup registry, so both register the key.
  - **CUDA graphs, batch invariance, spec decode.** See Dispatch above.
  - **Unchanged.** Prefill, the KV cache layout and checkpoints.

  **CI.** The new tests run in the optional (nightly) 4xB200 step, renamed "(4xB200) DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA Kernels" (`models_basic.yaml`, key `dsv41-nvidia-kernels-4xb200`), next to the specialized-decode tests. The kernel tests need SM10x, the FlashMLA mega ops and a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+, and skip otherwise; with vLLM's pinned `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0` they run. The optional "(B200)
  LM Eval Spec Decode" step runs the V4.1-Flash NVFP4 DSpark TP4 GSM8K config. It runs at full concurrency, where few steps are small enough for swap-AB.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched GitHub (open PRs plus PRs since 2026-08-15) for "swap-AB", "swapab", "small-head decode", "heads padded 64 decode", "mega attention DSv4.1" and "V4.1 decode attention". No PR adds an SM10x small-head decode
  kernel for the mega-attention path. Related work:
  - **#59418** (open, small-head sparse decode on SM90) is a Triton kernel for Hopper. It targets 8 or 16 heads in the plain FlashMLA sparse layer, which reads the 584 B `fp8_ds_mla` records used off SM10x. This PR targets SM10x tcgen05 and 16 or 32 heads
  in the mega-attention layer, which reads the V4.1 records and fuses the inverse RoPE and MXFP8 output.
  - **#61615** (open) is small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM90. This PR changes decode only, on SM10x.
  - **#57711** (closed by its author on 2026-09-25) was an opt-in split-KV mode inside the mega decode kernel, behind the `VLLM_DSV41_MEGA_SPLITKV` env flags and blocked on vllm-project/FlashMLA#25. That kernel still pads the heads to 64. This PR leaves
  FlashMLA alone, removes the padded-head work and adds no flags.
  - **#61868** (open) is an opt-in GB300 TP4 DSpark executor whose sparse-MLA decode uses FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4`. That is a separate opt-in path; this PR changes the default mega-attention path.

  **AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). It drafted the port of the kernel onto main, the tests, the benchmark arm, the `/pr-checklist` pass and this description. The submitter reviewed every changed

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""DeepSeek V4.1 swap-AB decode attention vs FlashMLA's mega kernel.
+
+The swap-AB kernel keeps the mega kernel's contract: it reads Q in the
+chunk-interleaved, head-padded layout and writes MXFP8 in the o-fused layout
+``wo_a`` reads, for the live heads' groups only. The caches are written by
+V4.1's own insert kernels, and both kernels are held to an fp64 reference over
+the dequantized records.
+"""
+
+import math
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion.quant_activation import QuantizedActivation
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops import quantize_and_insert_k_cache
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.fused_compress_quant_cache import (
+    rope_quant_insert,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.fused_layout import (
+    WV_GROUP_SIZE,
+    permute_q_to_fused,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia import flash_mla_mega_attn as mega_attn
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.flash_mla_mega_attn import (
+    _ROPE_ARGS,
+    _SF_ARGS,
+    DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention,
+    alloc_mega_attn_output,
+    is_flashmla_mega_attn_supported,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MLAAttentionSpec
+
+HEAD_DIM, ROPE_DIM = 512, 64
+NOPE_DIM = HEAD_DIM - ROPE_DIM
+FP8_RECORD, NVFP4_RECORD = 528, 288
+PADDED_HEADS = 64
+SCALE = HEAD_DIM**-0.5
+MAX_POS = 65536
+# V4.1-Flash's decode lists: the 128-slot window and 512 compressed slots.
+SWA_WIDTH, EXTRA_WIDTH = 128, 512
+# Slots per page: SWA, and compressed on ratio-2 layers (128 on ratio-1 ones).
+SWA_BLOCK, EXTRA_BLOCK = 32, 64
+SWA_SLOTS, EXTRA_SLOTS = 4096, 16384
+# A block also holds the other pages of its KV cache group, so a layer's pages
+# sit further apart than its records span. As in a packed block, the stride
+# stays a multiple of 512 B and of the record, which FlashMLA requires: it
+# reads the records as rows of the whole cache.
+PAD_RECORDS = 32
+E2M1_MAGNITUDES = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0)
+# Output bytes no kernel wrote: 448 in e4m3, 2**-1 as a ue8m0 scale.
+SENTINEL = 0x7E
+SENTINEL_WORD = 0x7E7E7E7E
+
+_MEGA_ATTN_SUPPORTED, _MEGA_ATTN_REASON = is_flashmla_mega_attn_supported()
+requires_mega_attn = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _MEGA_ATTN_SUPPORTED, reason=f"{_MEGA_ATTN_REASON}"
+)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Case:
+    heads: int
+    q: torch.Tensor  # [s_q, heads, 512] bf16, head-major
+    q_fused: torch.Tensor  # [s_q, 64, 512] bf16, zero-padded, chunk-interleaved
+    positions: torch.Tensor  # [s_q] int64
+    sink: torch.Tensor  # [64] fp32, -inf past the live heads

+    out = _asm(
+        llvm.StructType.get_literal([T.i32()] * 4),
+        [

+            _v(w1, Uint32, loc, ip),
+            _v(exponent, Uint32, loc, ip),

+        "mov.b32 {a0, a1}, $4;\n\tmov.b32 {a2, a3}, $5;\n\t"
+        "shl.b32 e2, $6, 8;\n\tor.b32 e2, e2, $6;\n\tcvt.u16.u32 sf, e2;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.scaled::n2::ue8m0.bf16x2.e4m3x2 $0, a0, sf;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.scaled::n2::ue8m0.bf16x2.e4m3x2 $1, a1, sf;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.scaled::n2::ue8m0.bf16x2.e4m3x2 $2, a2, sf;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.scaled::n2::ue8m0.bf16x2.e4m3x2 $3, a3, sf;\n\t}",
+        "=r,=r,=r,=r,r,r,r",

+        ip=ip,

+@dsl_user_op
+def _e4m3_to_bf16x2(byte, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Uint32:
+    """One e4m3 byte -> the same bf16 value in both halves of a word (exact)."""
+    b = Uint32(byte)
+    return Uint32(
+        _asm(
+            T.i32(),
+            [_v(b | (b << 8), Uint32, loc, ip)],
+            "{\n\t.reg .b16 x;\n\tcvt.u16.u32 x, $1;\n\t"
+            "cvt.rn.bf16x2.e4m3x2 $0, x;\n\t}",
+            "=r,r",
+            loc=loc,
+            ip=ip,
+        )
+    )

+@dsl_user_op
+def _fp4x8_to_bf16x8(w, scale_bf16x2, *, loc=None, ip=None):
+    """Eight e2m1 (even element in the low nibble) times a bf16 e4m3 scale.
+
+    e2m1 -> bf16 is exact and e2m1 * e4m3 has at most 6 significant bits, so the
+    bf16 product is exact: ``bf16(E2M1[code] * fp32(scale))``.
+    """
+    out = _asm(
+        llvm.StructType.get_literal([T.i32()] * 4),
+        [_v(w, Uint32, loc, ip), _v(scale_bf16x2, Uint32, loc, ip)],
+        "{\n\t.reg .b8 b0, b1, b2, b3;\n\t.reg .b32 h0, h1, h2, h3;\n\t"
+        "mov.b32 {b0, b1, b2, b3}, $4;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.e2m1x2 h0, b0;\n\tcvt.rn.bf16x2.e2m1x2 h1, b1;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.e2m1x2 h2, b2;\n\tcvt.rn.bf16x2.e2m1x2 h3, b3;\n\t"
+        "mul.rn.bf16x2 $0, h0, $5;\n\tmul.rn.bf16x2 $1, h1, $5;\n\t"
+        "mul.rn.bf16x2 $2, h2, $5;\n\tmul.rn.bf16x2 $3, h3, $5;\n\t}",
+        "=r,=r,=r,=r,r,r",
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+    return _fields(out, 4, T.i32(), Uint32, loc, ip)

+    """``_tcgen05.make_sdesc_128B_swizzle`` for the 16-head P tile's 64 B rows."""
+    return Uint64((SBO >> 4 << 32) | (1 << 46) | (4 << 61))

+    return Int32(cutlass.select_(cond, Int32(1), Int32(0)))

+def _sel(cond, a, b, ty):

+class SwapABDecodeKernel(VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel["SwapABDecodeKernel.CompileKey"]):
+    @dataclass(frozen=True)
+    class CompileKey:
+        heads: int  # live heads: 16 or 32
+        swa_width: int  # columns of the SWA slot list
+        extra_width: int  # columns of the compressed slot list
+        extra_record: int  # compressed record bytes: 528 (fp8) or 288 (NVFP4)
+        swa_page: int  # slots per SWA cache page
+        extra_page: int  # slots per compressed cache page

+    @staticmethod
+    def kernel(compile_key: CompileKey) -> Any:
+        H = compile_key.heads
+        assert H in (16, 32), "live heads must be 16 or 32"
+        NK, NE = compile_key.swa_width, compile_key.extra_width
+        assert compile_key.extra_record in (_FP8_RECORD, _FP4_RECORD), (
+            "compressed records must be V4.1 fp8 or NVFP4"
+        )
+        EXTRA_FP4 = compile_key.extra_record == _FP4_RECORD
+        KP, EP = compile_key.swa_page, compile_key.extra_page
+        for page in (KP, EP):
+            assert page > 0 and page & (page - 1) == 0, "page sizes must be powers of 2"
+        KT = cdiv(NK, _SWA_ROWS)
+        ET = cdiv(NE, _TILE)
+        C = KT + ET
+        assert 1 <= C <= _MAX_CLUSTER, f"{C} KV tiles per token > {_MAX_CLUSTER}"
+
+        NC = H // 4  # score / P columns per thread in the softmax
+        S_COL = 8 * H  # TMEM: O hi|lo for 4 M-blocks first, then S
+        TMEM_COLS = 256 if S_COL + H <= 256 else 512
+        P_ROW = 4 * H  # bytes per P row: H bf16 hi + H bf16 lo
+        Q_PIECES = H * _HEAD_DIM // 8  # 16-byte Q pieces
+        QP = Q_PIECES // _THREADS
+        assert QP * _THREADS == Q_PIECES
+        U = (_HEAD_DIM // 32) * H  # (head, 32-dim chunk) output units
+        UPC = cdiv(U, C)
+        NPASS = cdiv(UPC, _THREADS // 8)
+        STATS = C * 2 * H
+        UNIT_BYTES = 32 * 4  # one (head, 32-dim chunk) unit of the fp32 partial
+
+        IDESC_S = _tcgen05.make_bf16_idesc(_TILE, H)
+        IDESC_O = _tcgen05.make_bf16_idesc(
+            _TILE, 2 * H, transpose_A=True, transpose_B=True
+        )
+        DESC_KMAJ = _tcgen05.make_sdesc_128B_swizzle(0)
+        DESC_KV_MN = _tcgen05.make_sdesc_128B_swizzle(16384)
+        DESC_P = (
+            _tcgen05.make_sdesc_128B_swizzle(0)
+            if H == 32
+            else _make_sdesc_64B_swizzle(8 * P_ROW)
+        )
+        KB_Q = H * 128  # bytes per 64-dim k-block of Q
+
+        def stage_inputs(
+            fmt_fp4: bool,
+            cache,
+            idx,
+            lens,
+            q,
+            positions,
+            cos_sin,
+            b,
+            tid,
+            row0,
+            width: int,
+            page: int,
+            a_kv,
+            a_q,
+            a_valid,
+            a_cs,
+            rows: int,
+        ):
+            """Issue every global load, then Q RoPE -> SMEM and KV dequant -> SMEM.
+
+            ``rows`` (128 or 64) slots of the list start at ``row0``; with 64 the
+            tile's upper half is left unwritten and flagged invalid. Returns 1 if
+            the tile has any candidate slot (CTA-uniform).
+            """
+            page_shift = page.bit_length() - 1
+            row_bytes = 256 if fmt_fp4 else 512
+            sf_bytes = 32 if fmt_fp4 else 16
+            record = row_bytes + sf_bytes
+            # Gather mapping: TPR threads per row; lane % RPW = row within the warp,
+            # lane // RPW = part j, which owns 16-byte chunks j, j + TPR, ... .
+            TPR = _THREADS // rows
+            RPW = 32 // TPR
+            warp = tid // 32
+            lane = tid % 32
+            t = warp * RPW + lane % RPW
+            j = lane // RPW
+
+            # Slot ids do not wait for the length (one dependent round trip less).
+            rowpos = row0 + t
+            id_addr = (
+                idx.iterator.toint()
+                + (Int64(b) * Int64(idx.stride[0]) + Int64(rowpos)) * 4
+            )
+            sid = _ldg_s32(id_addr, _i32(rowpos < width), Int32(-1))
+            limit = cutlass.min(lens[b], Int32(width))
+            pos = positions[b]
+            live = row0 < limit
+            in_range = rowpos < limit
+

+            # q[b, (d // 16) * HP * 16 + h * 16 + d % 16]; only the last piece of a
+            # thread can reach the RoPE dims (static, see QP).
+            hp = Int64(q.shape[1])
+            q_base = q.iterator.toint() + Int64(b) * Int64(q.stride[0]) * 2
+            qw = []
+            qmeta = []
+            for k in range(QP):
+                i = tid + _THREADS * k
+                c16 = i // (2 * H)
+                rem = i % (2 * H)

+                half = rem % 2

+            # TPR * 16 contiguous bytes of each of its rows.
+            n_chunks = (row_bytes // 16) // TPR
+            kv = []
+            for k in range(n_chunks):

+            # than the slot ids). The whole row also goes to SMEM for the epilogue.
+            d_last = qmeta[QP - 1][0]
+            rope = d_last >= _ROPE_START
+            f0 = (d_last - _ROPE_START) // 2
+            cs_row = (
+                cos_sin.iterator.toint() + Int64(pos) * Int64(cos_sin.stride[0]) * 4
+            )
+            cosv = _ldg_f32x4(cs_row + Int64(f0) * 4, _i32(rope), 1.0)
+            sinv = _ldg_f32x4(cs_row + Int64(f0 + _ROPE_DIM // 2) * 4, _i32(rope), 0.0)
+            cs_lane = tid % 16
+            cs_pred = _i32(tid < 16)
+            csw = _ldg_v4(cs_row + Int64(cs_lane) * 16, cs_pred)
+
+            # Q RoPE (fp32, GPT-J pairs) -> bf16 -> SMEM [H, 512] K-major SW128.
+            for k in range(QP):
+                d0, h = qmeta[k]
+                words = list(qw[k])
+                if k == QP - 1:
+                    for w in range(4):
+                        qe, qo = cvt.bf16x2_to_fp32x2(words[w])
+                        c, s = cosv[w], sinv[w]
+                        re = _fma(qe, c, -_mul(qo, s))
+                        ro = _fma(qo, c, _mul(qe, s))
+                        words[w] = _sel(
+                            rope, cvt.fp32x2_to_bf16x2(re, ro), words[w], Uint32
+                        )
+                kb = d0 // 64
+                phys = ((d0 % 64) // 8) ^ (h % 8)
+                addr = a_q + kb * KB_Q + (h // 8) * 1024 + (h % 8) * 128 + phys * 16
+                _sts_v4(addr, words[0], words[1], words[2], words[3])
+
+            # KV dequant -> SMEM [128, 512] bf16, K-major SW128 (8 k-blocks of
+            # 128 rows x 128 B; 16-byte chunk c of row r stored at c ^ (r % 8)).
+            row_off = a_kv + (t // 8) * 1024 + (t % 8) * 128
+            if fmt_fp4:
+                # NVFP4: 16-byte chunk c = TPR k + j holds dims [32 c, 32 c + 32); its
+                # e4m3 scales are bytes 2 c and 2 c + 1 of the record's 32 scale
+                # bytes, i.e. word TPR / 2 * k + j // 2.
+                for k in range(n_chunks):
+                    c = TPR * k + j
+                    kb_off = row_off + (c // 2) * 16384
+                    lc0 = (c % 2) * 4
+                    word = sfw[(TPR // 2) * k]
+                    for jj in range(1, TPR // 2):
+                        word = _sel(
+                            j // 2 == jj, sfw[(TPR // 2) * k + jj], word, Uint32
+                        )
+                    sh = Uint32((j % 2) * 16)
+                    s0 = _e4m3_to_bf16x2((word >> sh) & Uint32(0xFF))
+                    s1 = _e4m3_to_bf16x2((word >> (sh + Uint32(8))) & Uint32(0xFF))
+                    for w in range(4):
+                        o = _fp4x8_to_bf16x8(kv[k][w], s0 if w < 2 else s1)
+                        _sts_v4(
+                            kb_off + ((lc0 + w) ^ (t % 8)) * 16, o[0], o[1], o[2], o[3]
+                        )
+            else:
+                # fp8: 16-byte chunk c = TPR k + j holds dims [16 c, 16 c + 16) (k-block
+                # c // 4, 16-byte SMEM chunks 2 (j % 4) + {0, 1}), scaled by ue8m0 byte
+                # g = c // 2 = TPR / 2 * k + j // 2 of the record's 16 scale bytes.
+                for k in range(n_chunks):
+                    c = TPR * k + j
+                    kb_off = row_off + (c // 4) * 16384
+                    g0 = (TPR // 2) * k  # static part of g; j // 2 adds 0..TPR/2-1
+                    e = (
+                        sfw[g0 // 4] >> Uint32(8 * (g0 % 4)) >> Uint32(8 * (j // 2))
+                    ) & Uint32(0xFF)
+                    for w in range(2):
+                        o = _fp8x8_to_bf16x8_ue8m0(kv[k][2 * w], kv[k][2 * w + 1], e)
+                        _sts_v4(
+                            kb_off + ((2 * (j % 4) + w) ^ (t % 8)) * 16,
+                            o[0],
+                            o[1],
+                            o[2],
+                            o[3],
+                        )
+            _sts_s32(a_valid + t * 4, vp)
+            if rows < _TILE:  # the unwritten rows never take part
+                _sts_s32(a_valid + (rows + tid % (_TILE - rows)) * 4, Int32(0))
+            _sts_v4p(a_cs + cs_lane * 16, csw[0], csw[1], csw[2], csw[3], cs_pred)
+            return _i32(live)

+                row = []
+                for qp in cutlass.range_constexpr(C):

+                pulls.append(row)
+            for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(cdiv(STATS, _THREADS)):
+                i = cutlass.min(tid + _THREADS * k, Int32(STATS - 1))

+            cute.arch.sync_threads()
+
+            # ---- 9: merge this CTA's (head, 32-dim chunk) units (fixed peer order:
+            # deterministic; sink folded once), then the epilogue: inverse RoPE,
+            # MXFP8 cast, o-fused store.
+            out_base = out.iterator.toint() + Int64(b) * Int64(out.stride[0])
+            sf_base = out_sf.iterator.toint()
+            inf = Float32(math.inf)
+            for ps in cutlass.range_constexpr(NPASS):
+                uo = ps * (_THREADS // 8) + tid // 8
+                active = uo < u_count
+                uoc = cutlass.min(uo, u_count - 1)
+                u = u_begin + uoc
+                hh = u // 16
+                cc = u % 16
+                sk = sink[hh]
+                sk2 = sk * _LOG2E
+                parts = pulls[ps]
+                ms = []
+                ls = []
+                big = sk2
+                for qp in cutlass.range_constexpr(C):
+                    mq = _lds_f32(a_stat_all + (qp * 2 * H + hh) * 4)
+                    lq = _lds_f32(a_stat_all + (qp * 2 * H + H + hh) * 4)
+                    ms.append(mq)
+                    ls.append(lq)
+                    big = _sel(lq > Float32(0.0), cute.arch.fmax(big, mq), big, Float32)
+                big = _sel((big == inf) | (big == -inf), Float32(0.0), big, Float32)
+                den = _ex2(sk2 - big)
+                acc = [Float32(0.0)] * 4
+                for qp in cutlass.range_constexpr(C):
+                    f = _sel(
+                        ls[qp] > Float32(0.0), _ex2(ms[qp] - big), Float32(0.0), Float32

+                    den = den + f * ls[qp]

+                        acc[e] = acc[e] + parts[qp][e] * f
+                ok = (den > Float32(0.0)) & (sk != inf)
+                for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                    acc[e] = _sel(ok, acc[e] / den, Float32(0.0), Float32)
+                if cutlass.const_expr(ps == NPASS - 1):
+                    # Every pulled value is consumed: peers may leave once all of
+                    # them got here too (split barrier, waited on before exit).
+                    cute.arch.cluster_arrive_relaxed()
+                # Inverse GPT-J RoPE on dims >= 448 (identity elsewhere).
+                is_rope = cc >= _ROPE_START // 32
+                f0 = cutlass.max((cc - _ROPE_START // 32) * 16 + sub * 2, Int32(0))
+                cs2 = _lds_v2f(a_cs + f0 * 4)
+                sn2 = _lds_v2f(a_cs + (f0 + _ROPE_DIM // 2) * 4)
+                x = []
+                for pr in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                    cv = _sel(is_rope, cs2[pr], Float32(1.0), Float32)
+                    sv1 = _sel(is_rope, sn2[pr], Float32(0.0), Float32)
+                    oe, oo = acc[2 * pr], acc[2 * pr + 1]
+                    x.append(_fma(oe, cv, _mul(sv1, oo)))
+                    x.append(_fma(oo, cv, -_mul(sv1, oe)))
+                # MXFP8: ue8m0 = ceil(log2(amax / 448)) over the 32-dim chunk.
+                amax = cute.arch.fmax(
+                    cute.arch.fmax(
+                        cute.arch.fmax(x[0], -x[0]), cute.arch.fmax(x[1], -x[1])
+                    ),
+                    cute.arch.fmax(
+                        cute.arch.fmax(x[2], -x[2]), cute.arch.fmax(x[3], -x[3])
+                    ),
+                )
+                for off in (4, 2, 1):
+                    amax = cute.arch.fmax(
+                        amax, cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(amax, offset=off)
+                    )
+                amax = cute.arch.fmax(amax, Float32(1e-10))
+                ex = _ue8m0_rp(amax * Float32(1.0 / 448.0))
+                inv = recast_val((Uint32(254) - ex) << Uint32(23), Float32)
+                qb = cvt.fp32x4_to_fp8x4(x[0] * inv, x[1] * inv, x[2] * inv, x[3] * inv)
+                g = hh // WV_GROUP_SIZE
+                hg = hh % WV_GROUP_SIZE
+                ka = cc * WV_GROUP_SIZE + hg
+                oa = (
+                    out_base
+                    + Int64(g) * Int64(out.stride[1])
+                    + Int64(ka * 32 + sub * 4)
+                )
+                _stg_b32(oa, qb, _i32(active))
+                sw_idx = (
+                    Int64(b) * Int64(out_sf.stride[0])
+                    + Int64(g) * Int64(out_sf.stride[1])
+                    + Int64(ka // 4) * Int64(out_sf.stride[2])
+                )
+                _stg_b8(
+                    sf_base + sw_idx * 4 + Int64(ka % 4), ex, _i32(active & (sub == 0))
+                )
+
+            # ---- 10: nobody leaves while a peer may still read its SMEM (the
+            # matching arrive follows this CTA's last pull).
+            cute.arch.cluster_wait()

+                cute.arch.dealloc_tmem(

+        def host_entrypoint(
+            q: cute.Tensor,
+            swa: cute.Tensor,
+            swa_idx: cute.Tensor,
+            swa_len: cute.Tensor,
+            ext: cute.Tensor,

+                swa_len,
+                ext,

+                ext_len,
+                positions,
+                cos_sin,
+                sink,
+                out,
+                out_sf,
+                scale_log2,
+            ).launch(
+                grid=(C, q.shape[0], 1),
+                block=(_THREADS, 1, 1),
+                cluster=(C, 1, 1),
+                stream=stream,
+                use_pdl=True,
+                # 150+ KiB of SMEM leaves room for one CTA per SM anyway; saying

+
+    def dispatch(self, **compile_key_fields: int) -> CompileKey:
+        return self.CompileKey(**compile_key_fields)
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(self, **layer_shape: int) -> list[CompileKey]:
+        # The token count is a grid dimension, so one executor per layer shape
+        # serves every decode step.
+        return self._trace_dispatch(self.dispatch)(**layer_shape)
+
+    def warmup_inputs(self, compile_key: CompileKey) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+        def cache(page: int, record: int):
+            return make_fake_tensor(
+                Uint8,
+                (cute.sym_int(), page, record),
+                (cute.sym_int(), record, 1),
+                assumed_align=16,
+            )
+
+        # Independent leading dims: metadata buffers may be longer than s_q.
+        def slots(width: int):
+            return make_fake_tensor(
+                Int32, (cute.sym_int(), width), (cute.sym_int(), 1), assumed_align=4
+            )
+
+        def vec(dtype):
+            return make_fake_tensor(dtype, (cute.sym_int(),), (1,), assumed_align=4)
+
+        out_dim = WV_GROUP_SIZE * _HEAD_DIM
+        return (
+            make_fake_tensor(
+                BFloat16,
+                (cute.sym_int(), cute.sym_int(), _HEAD_DIM),
+                (cute.sym_int(), _HEAD_DIM, 1),
+                assumed_align=16,
+            ),
+            cache(compile_key.swa_page, _FP8_RECORD),
+            slots(compile_key.swa_width),
+            vec(Int32),
+            cache(compile_key.extra_page, compile_key.extra_record),
+            slots(compile_key.extra_width),
+            vec(Int32),
+            make_fake_tensor(Int64, (cute.sym_int(),), (1,), assumed_align=8),
+            make_fake_tensor(
+                Float32,
+                (cute.sym_int(), _ROPE_DIM),
+                (cute.sym_int(), 1),
+                assumed_align=16,
+            ),
+            vec(Float32),
+            make_fake_tensor(
+                Float8E4M3FN,
+                (cute.sym_int(), cute.sym_int(), out_dim),
+                (cute.sym_int(), out_dim, 1),
+                assumed_align=16,
+            ),
+            make_fake_tensor(
+                Int32,
+                (cute.sym_int(), cute.sym_int(), out_dim // 128),
+                (cute.sym_int(), cute.sym_int(), cute.sym_int()),
+                assumed_align=4,
+            ),
+            Float32(0.0),
+        )
+
+    @kernel_launcher
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        swa_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        swa_idx: torch.Tensor,
+        swa_len: torch.Tensor,
+        extra_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        extra_idx: torch.Tensor,
+        extra_len: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        sink: torch.Tensor,
+        heads: int,
+        softmax_scale: float,
+        out_data: torch.Tensor,
+        out_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> CuTeDSLLaunchSpec["SwapABDecodeKernel.CompileKey"]:
+        """Decode attention of ``heads`` live heads, in place into ``out_*``.
+
+        The arguments are those of the mega kernel's decode call: ``q`` is
+        ``[s_q, padded_heads, 512]`` bf16 in its chunk-interleaved layout, not
+        yet RoPEd; the caches are ``[num_blocks, page, record]`` uint8 views
+        of V4.1 records (a token's data, then its scales) whose pages may be
+        further apart than ``page * record`` bytes; the slot lists are
+        ``[s_q, width]`` int32 slot ids (``block * page + offset``, ``-1``
+        invalid) with ``[s_q]`` int32 lengths; ``positions`` is int64. Only
+        the live heads' groups of ``out_data`` / ``out_scale`` are written.
+        """
+        assert q.shape[1] >= heads
+        compile_key = self.dispatch(
+            heads=heads,
+            swa_width=swa_idx.shape[-1],
+            extra_width=extra_idx.shape[-1],
+            extra_record=extra_cache.shape[-1],
+            swa_page=swa_cache.shape[1],
+            extra_page=extra_cache.shape[1],
+        )
+        launch_args = (
+            q,
+            swa_cache,
+            swa_idx,
+            swa_len,
+            extra_cache,
+            extra_idx,
+            extra_len,
+            positions,
+            cos_sin_cache,
+            sink,
+            out_data,
+            out_scale,
+            softmax_scale * _LOG2E,
+        )
+        return compile_key, launch_args
+
+
+def swapab_decode_supported(heads: int, swa_width: int, extra_width: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether the kernel serves these live heads and slot-list widths.
+
+    A token's KV tiles have to fit one portable cluster, and the fp8 / fp4 ->
+    bf16 conversions need PTX ISA 9.2, i.e. a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+.
+    """
+    tiles = cdiv(swa_width, _SWA_ROWS) + cdiv(extra_width, _TILE)
+    return (
+        heads in (16, 32)
+        and 1 <= tiles <= _MAX_CLUSTER
+        and target_version(min_version="13.2")
+    )
+
+
+_SWAPAB_DECODE_KERNEL = SwapABDecodeKernel()

Server: `vllm serve` with `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`, `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'`, `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`, `--max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching`; TP2 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, TP4 with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`. Load: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512`, no spec decode, so decode steps carry exactly `concurrency` tokens; c64 is the above-gate parity point.

**Median TPOT (ms), stock → PR:**

| Concurrency | TP2 fp8 | Δ | TP4 NVFP4 | Δ |
| ---: | :---: | ---: | :---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.89 → 4.46 | **−8.8%** | 3.91 → 3.71 | **−5.1%** |
| 2 | 5.47 → 4.98 | **−9.0%** | 4.28 → 4.04 | **−5.6%** |
| 4 | 5.96 → 5.46 | **−8.4%** | 4.66 → 4.39 | **−5.8%** |
| 8 | 7.08 → 6.58 | **−7.1%** | 5.35 → 5.13 | **−4.1%** |
| 16 | 8.96 → 8.56 | **−4.5%** | 6.67 → 6.53 | **−2.1%** |
| 64 (above gate) | 16.58 → 16.85 | +1.6% | 12.91 → 13.05 | +1.1% |

Inside the gate the win shrinks as concurrency grows, as expected (attention is a shrinking share of the step). At c64 both arms run only the mega kernel; the +1.1–1.6% there reads as run noise — two reruns of the PR arm's TP2 c64 on another node gave 16.81/16.83 ms with clean means, and I'm happy to pin it down further if you'd like. E2E TPOT gains are, as expected, much smaller than the 1.6–2.15x per-layer attention-step numbers in the description.

**GSM8K** (lm-eval `local-completions`, 5-shot strict-match, all 1319 questions, `num_concurrent=8` so decode steps stay inside the gate):

| | stock | this PR |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| TP2 fp8 | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9227 ± 0.0074 |
| TP4 NVFP4 | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9249 ± 0.0073 |

Both deltas are within one standard error and within this model's run-to-run spread on GSM8K (e.g. the `main` spread reported on #63018 was 0.9249–0.9356); the engine is not run-deterministic at these settings, and the PR's fp64-reference unit tests bound the kernel-level error.

**Correction to the 10/28 numbers, and a re-run on current main.**

1. **The 10/28 "TP2 fp8" rows were NVFP4 records.** On this layer `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` resolves to the packed `nvfp4_ds_mla` format; fp8 compressed records need `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`. So the TP2 TPOT column and the TP2 GSM8K row of that comment measured NVFP4 records. The TP4 column was NVFP4 as labeled.
2. **Merge break, fixed in 176da21.** After #61971, the merged branch still passed the removed `positions_int32` to the swap-AB kernel. The kernel input, layer call, benchmark and tests now take the int64 positions. Everything below is on that head.

**Re-run.** B300, vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2` (includes #61971); stock vs stock plus this PR's `vllm/` diff; TP2; flags as on 10/28 except `--kv-cache-dtype`. One job on one node ran the arms back to back: fp8_ds_mla stock → PR, nvfp4_ds_mla stock → PR, then that sequence again. No failed requests.

**Median TPOT (ms), stock → PR:**

| Concurrency | fp8_ds_mla rep 1 | fp8_ds_mla rep 2 | Δ | nvfp4_ds_mla rep 1 | nvfp4_ds_mla rep 2 | Δ |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | ---: | :---: | :---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.96 → 4.58 | 4.95 → 4.58 | **−7.6%** | 5.01 → 4.55 | 5.00 → 4.82 | **−6.4%** |
| 2 | 5.42 → 5.03 | 5.41 → 5.05 | **−6.9%** | 5.46 → 4.99 | 5.44 → 5.32 | **−5.4%** |
| 4 | 5.93 → 5.55 | 5.92 → 5.54 | **−6.4%** | 6.01 → 5.56 | 6.02 → 5.56 | **−7.6%** |
| 8 | 7.03 → 6.60 | 7.07 → 6.61 | **−6.3%** | 7.11 → 6.66 | 7.12 → 6.65 | **−6.5%** |
| 16 | 8.89 → 8.40 | 8.87 → 8.55 | **−4.6%** | 8.98 → 8.56 | 8.96 → 8.53 | **−4.7%** |

Δ is the change in the summed TPOT of both repeats.

- **Spread.** Stock repeats agree within 0.04 ms. PR repeats agree within 0.15 ms, except NVFP4 rep 2 at c1/c2 (4.82/5.32 vs 4.55/4.99). In that window per-request TPOT was uniform (p99 equal to the median), and the same server measured 5.56 ms again at c4, so I've kept it in the average rather than dropping it. An earlier fp8_ds_mla pair on this image gave c1 4.87 → 4.51 and c16 8.89 → 8.41.
- **Same gain for both record formats.** This matches the kernel microbenchmark, where swap-AB saves about the same time per layer for 288 B and 528 B records.
- **Dispatch check.** A measurement-only logging probe in every server confirmed that each decode step of 1-16 tokens ran swap-AB on the compressed layers in the PR arm, for both formats. Only the pure-SWA layers (`compress_ratio == 0`) kept the mega kernel, by design.
- **Above the gate.** At c64 both arms run the mega kernel. One earlier pair on this image differed by +0.7% (fp8_ds_mla) and +4.1% (NVFP4); this is run-to-run noise at that point, not an effect of the PR.
- **Older image.** One earlier fp8_ds_mla pair on the older `00b6c4c5` image, run without the dispatch probe, showed a smaller gain (−1.6% at c1, parity at c16). I haven't reproduced that on the current image, so I'm not drawing on it.

**GSM8K, fp8_ds_mla at TP2** (same settings as 10/28: 5-shot strict-match, all 1319 questions, `num_concurrent=8` so decode steps stay inside the gate): stock 0.9295 → PR 0.9325.

**Kernel level on B300.** The description's benchmark gives 1.83-2.0x with 16 heads and 1.41-1.64x with 32 heads at 1-16 tokens, for both record formats. That is below the 1.6-1.8x the description claimed for TP2, so I've updated the description to give the B300 range.
